decisions.decision: Keep the KnowledgeDataEngine provider boundary in OpenCTI and the OpenCTI-to-generic-graph mapping in the dedicated Corrobore CTI adapter, outside graph-core.
decisions.rationale: OpenCTI owns routing and removal of direct client access, while Corrobore remains domain-neutral and the existing CTI domain boundary remains reusable.

decisions.decision: Capture normalized requests and results at the KnowledgeDataEngine boundary; until that boundary lands, instrument the catalogued engine helper exports rather than the low-level HTTP transport.
decisions.rationale: Logical captures preserve user, tenant and ordering semantics without binding the corpus to Elasticsearch wire details.

decisions.decision: Require read-your-writes for an acknowledged mutation and snapshot-consistent pagination identified by a transaction version.
decisions.rationale: This is the minimum model that prevents duplicates or omissions across pages while keeping rebuildable secondary indexes behind one WAL.

decisions.decision: Use Tantivy as the embedded full-text index behind a Corrobore-owned search abstraction.
decisions.rationale: Tantivy is Rust-native and supports the inverted-index, phrase, fuzzy, scoring and filtering primitives required by the PRD without exposing its API in the public engine contract.

decisions.decision: Run file extraction in a dedicated sandboxed worker; persist extracted text and its searchable index in Corrobore.
decisions.rationale: PDF, office and HTML parsers expand the security and dependency surface, while the PRD explicitly allows a separate worker but requires Corrobore to own indexing and results.

decisions.decision: Define one portable snapshot format produced locally and stream the same artifact through a storage abstraction to S3 or MinIO.
decisions.rationale: One integrity-checked format avoids divergent local and object-store restore paths and covers single-node development plus production backup.

decisions.decision: Phase parity covers count, cardinality, terms, date_histogram, sum, filter, nested and reverse_nested; min, max and avg remain PRD capabilities but are added only when an OpenCTI callsite or accepted dashboard fixture requires them.
decisions.rationale: The pinned OpenCTI source uses exactly this subset. It satisfies the no-full-Elasticsearch-emulation principle while the drift guard exposes future additions.

decisions.decision: Small is 100000 objects and 500000 relationships; medium is 1000000 objects and 5000000 relationships. Large remains outside phase 0.
decisions.rationale: These are the PRD benchmark thresholds and correspond to developer/small-organization and standard-production workloads.
